subject: forensic-medicine
title: Identification: Sex Determination from Skull, Pelvis and Dactylography

steps.title: Forensic hierarchy and accuracy in skeletal sex determination
steps.tx: When skeletonized or mutilated human remains are discovered, determining biological sex represents the cornerstone of personal identification. Forensic anthropologists follow a well-defined **skeletal sex determination accuracy hierarchy**: the pelvis alone yields ninety-five percent accuracy, the cranium alone provides ninety to ninety-two percent accuracy, the pelvis and skull combined achieve ninety-eight percent, and the complete skeleton provides ninety-nine to one hundred percent certainty.
steps.say: The pelvis alone determines skeletal sex with ninety-five percent accuracy, the skull gives ninety percent, and both together yield ninety-eight percent certainty.

steps.title: Cranial morphological dimorphism: Vault and supraorbital ridges
steps.tx: In osteological examination, **cranial sexual dimorphism characteristics** distinguish male and female crania through architectural mass and muscle markings. Male skulls are heavier, larger, and more rugged, displaying prominent sloping foreheads with pronounced supraorbital ridges and blunt orbital margins. In contrast, female skulls are smaller and smoother, characterized by vertical frontal bones with prominent parietal eminences, smooth supraorbital glabellae, and sharp superior orbital margins.
steps.say: Male skulls are larger and rugged with prominent brow ridges and sloping foreheads, whereas female skulls are smoother with vertical foreheads and sharp orbital rims.

right.title: Female cranium
points: Vertical forehead with distinct frontal eminences

steps.tx: Sexing a dry skull rests on **cranial sexual dimorphism characteristics** of mass and muscle marking. Male crania are heavier, larger, and more rugged, with sloping foreheads, strong supraorbital ridges, and blunt orbital margins. Female crania are smaller and smoother, with a vertical frontal bone, prominent parietal eminences, a flat glabella, and sharp superior orbital margins. No single ridge decides sex, but the set of forehead, brow, and orbital features is read together.
steps.say: Male skulls are heavier and rugged, with sloping foreheads, strong brow ridges, and blunt orbital rims. Female skulls are smoother, with vertical foreheads, parietal bosses, and sharp orbital margins.

steps.title: Mastoid process, occipital protuberance and mandibular features
steps.tx: The base and lower jaw display distinct dimorphism through **mastoid and mandibular sexual landmarks**. The male mastoid process is massive and broad; when rested on a flat table, the male skull rests stably on its mastoid processes. Male skulls exhibit prominent external occipital protuberances (inion hooks), square chins, and flared mandibular gonial angles, whereas female mastoids are small, occipital bones smooth, and chins pointed or rounded.
steps.say: Male skulls have large mastoid processes that rest flat on a table, prominent occipital hooks, and square jaws with flared gonial angles.

steps.title: Pelvic sexual dimorphism and reproductive adaptation
steps.tx: Reflecting evolutionary adaptation for childbearing, the **pelvic sexual dimorphism architecture** offers the most definitive skeletal evidence of sex. The female pelvis is broad, shallow, and spacious, featuring an open cylindrical cavity that facilitates fetal passage. Conversely, the male pelvis is heavy, deep, conical, and narrow, featuring prominent muscular crests and robust sacroiliac joint articulations designed for bipedal locomotion.
steps.say: The female pelvis is wide, shallow, and cylindrical for childbearing, while the male pelvis is narrow, deep, conical, and heavily built.

vis.alt: Diagram showing pelvic shapes, subpubic angle, and pelvic inlet variations between male and female pelvis
vis.caption: Pelvic sexual dimorphism: The female gynecoid pelvis demonstrates a wide obtuse subpubic angle, spacious circular inlet, and wide greater sciatic notch compared to the narrow male android pelvis. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.title: Pelvic inlet contours and subpubic arch morphology
steps.tx: Diagnostic differentiation focuses on the **subpubic angle and pelvic inlet** contours. In females, the subpubic angle is obtuse and rounded, exceeding eighty to ninety degrees to form a broad inverted U-shaped arch. In males, the subpubic arch is acute and V-shaped, measuring sixty to seventy degrees. Furthermore, the female pelvic inlet is transversely oval or circular, whereas the male inlet is heart-shaped (android).
steps.say: The female subpubic arch forms a wide U-shape over eighty-five degrees with an oval inlet, while the male arch forms a narrow V-shape under seventy degrees.

right.title: Female pelvis (Gynecoid)
points: Pelvic inlet: Broad, transversely oval / circular

steps.tx: Sex of an isolated hip bone is read from the **subpubic angle and pelvic inlet**. The female subpubic angle is obtuse and rounded, more than eighty to ninety degrees, forming a broad inverted U. The male arch is acute and V shaped, about sixty to seventy degrees. The female inlet is transversely oval or nearly circular, while the male inlet is heart shaped, the android form. These contours are judged on the dried innominate, not on soft tissue.
steps.say: On the hip bone the female pubic arch is a wide U beyond about eighty five degrees, with an oval or round inlet. The male arch is a narrow V of sixty to seventy degrees and the inlet is heart shaped.

vis.alt: Isolated male and female innominate bones are set side by side to compare the greater sciatic notch.
vis.caption: Male and female hip bones lie together so the greater sciatic notch and the pubic arch can be compared. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: The greater sciatic notch and preauricular sulcus
steps.tx: On the posterior ilium, the **greater sciatic notch index** serves as a vital dimorphic criterion. The female notch is broad, spacious, and shallow, forming an angle of approximately sixty degrees with a high width-to-depth index. The male notch is narrow and deep, forming an acute angle under thirty degrees. Adjacent to the notch, a deep preauricular paraglenoid sulcus commonly indents the female ilium, representing ligamentous remodeling from pregnancy.
steps.say: The greater sciatic notch is wide and shallow in females, and narrow and deep in males. A deep preauricular groove reflects pregnancy and female pelvic anatomy.

steps.title: Washburn ischiopubic index and sacral dimorphism
steps.tx: Anthropologists employ the quantitative **Washburn ischiopubic index formula** to establish sex objectively. Calculated by dividing pubic length by ischial length and multiplying by one hundred, females score between ninety and one hundred, whereas males score below eighty-four. Concurrently, the female sacrum is short, broad, and curved predominantly in its lower third, compared to the long, narrow, evenly curved male sacrum.
steps.say: The Washburn index divides pubic by ischial length: females score over ninety, while males score under eighty-four. Female sacra are shorter and broader.

steps.title: Sex determination through fingerprint epidermal ridge density
steps.tx: When skin fragments or decomposed hands survive, **fingerprint epidermal ridge density** provides dermatoglyphic clues to biological sex. Because females possess finer dermal papillary ridges, they exhibit significantly higher ridge density within a defined area compared to males. Counting ridges within a standard twenty-five-square-millimeter upper radial quadrant reveals over thirteen to fourteen ridges in females, compared to eleven to twelve ridges in males.
steps.say: Fingerprint ridge density aids sex determination: females have finer ridges with over thirteen ridges per standard square, compared to under twelve in males.

steps.title: Cellular sex chromatin and Barr body demonstration
steps.tx: In fresh tissue fragments, dental pulp, or mucosal smears, cytogeneticists confirm genetic sex through **sex chromatin Barr body demonstration**. In females (XX), the inactive condensed X chromosome appears as a dark, plano-convex, Feulgen-positive mass measuring one micron against the inner nuclear membrane of interphase cells in twenty to sixty percent of nuclei, whereas male cells (XY) possess fewer than two percent Barr bodies.
steps.say: Barr bodies represent condensed inactive X chromosomes, found in over twenty percent of female nuclei in dental pulp or skin, and absent in normal males.
